posts.text:
Police came to check on a 28-year-old nurse who hadn't shown up for work. Her husband opened the door holding their baby. By then, prosecutors say, she had been dead for three days and her body had been cut apart and thrown out with the trash. Calmly, he told the officer:

"She destroyed that phone, and then she left." She was going to New York or Texas, according to him. He wanted to know if he'd have to file a complaint. And there was something else: she had "mental issues." Two years later, on the witness stand, he finally said it out loud:

"I had a saw, I used the saw." Naresh Bhatt says he found his wife Mamta dead in their bedroom, panicked and cut her apart. In his version she took her own life. He denies killing her.

July 2024, Manassas Park, Virginia. Mamta Kafle Bhatt was a nurse from Nepal and a new mother. Prosecutors say she was killed at home on or about July 30. The next afternoon, cameras at a Walmart filmed her husband buying carpet cleaner, cleaning supplies and body wash.

He didn't want to report her missing, and only did it three days after the police visit. On August 22 he was arrested for concealing a dead body while she was still, officially, a missing person. That December came the first-degree murder charge.

Her remains have never been found. Investigators say blood on a power saw likely matches her DNA. For two years he said he had no idea what happened to her. Now he admits to the saw and the trash bags, and insists the one thing he didn't do is kill her. The jury could get the case this week.

In the video below is the police bodycam from August 2. He holds the baby the whole time. She wouldn't see a psychiatrist, he says, because in her words, "I'm a registered nurse." When the officer asks him to call if she comes back, he answers: "Until Sunday, I don't think so." Then the clip cuts to the courtroom.

Three days, one saw, two years of "she left." A panicked husband, or a man who waited two years for a better story?

posts.text:
We are saddened by the passing of Bob Boone, part of one of baseball’s most historic families. 

Along with his father Ray, and his sons Bret and Aaron, the Boones became the first family to field three generations of Major League players, all of them All-Stars. 

Bob, a catcher who came up in 1972, played 19 Major League seasons with the Phillies, Angels, and Royals. When he retired after the 1990 season, he had caught 2,225 games, the most in MLB history at that time. 

A four-time All-Star, Boone was an elite defender, winning 7 Gold Gloves. He won his last in 1989 at age 41 and remains the oldest position player to win a Gold Glove. 

Boone’s leadership behind the plate helped his teams reach the Postseason seven times from 1976-86. In the 1980 World Series, he batted .412 with 4 RBIs to help the Phillies win their first championship in franchise history. 

Boone later managed six seasons with the Royals and Reds before spending more than a decade as a front office executive with the Washington Nationals, a run that included their first World Series title in 2019. 

He was 78.

And now, for your grand fucking finale, you’re counting “eight impeachable acts” like some pious little altar boy with a hard-on for losing, because Pete Hegseth is effective, the war is going the way your voters wanted, and your colleagues aren’t stupid enough to follow a lame-duck loser into a political suicide pact.

Eight! EIGHT! Congratulations, you sanctimonious dipshit. Did you count them all by yourself, or did you need your Democrat buddies to take your shoes off so you could get past ten?

And since you've suddenly appointed yourself the nation's supreme authority on military accountability, let's revisit Lloyd fucking Austin.

The Secretary of Defense vanished into a hospital for days, the President wasn't informed, his own deputy didn't know the full circumstances, and the Pentagon's chain of command looked like a goddamn Three Stooges reunion.

WHERE THE FUCK WAS CAPTAIN ACCOUNTABILITY THEN, YOU SPINELESS, TWO-FACED LITTLE SHITSTAIN?

No impeachment crusade. No constitutional sermon. No theatrical outrage. Apparently your principles were buried somewhere between your pinecone collection and whatever Democrat's ass you were kissing that week.

But Hegseth starts kicking ass, and suddenly the mighty Thomas Massie emerges from his woodland fucking monastery, clutching his impeachment articles like Moses descending Mount Sinai, ready to lecture everybody about constitutional responsibility.

Spare me the sanctimonious horseshit, you gutless fraud.

You've become the Democrats' favorite useful Republican, a pompous, backstabbing jackass who mistakes sabotaging his own party for some grand demonstration of moral superiority. You're the political equivalent of a hemorrhoid that learned to quote the Federalist Papers.

And the funniest fucking part? Kentucky finally saw through the act.

After years of listening to you congratulate yourself for being the smartest, bravest, most principled man in Washington, your own voters apparently decided they'd rather have an empty fucking chair than another term of your insufferable bullshit.

Imagine possessing an ego so catastrophically inflated that getting your ass handed to you at the ballot box only convinces you the country desperately needs MORE of your unsolicited wisdom.

So here's some advice, Tommy.

Go clear out your empty office, go fuck yourself with that pinecone on the way out, and take your resume full of nothing with you.

You're a pathetic, irrelevant, treasonous clown who peaked as a meme, and your greatest congressional accomplishment was demonstrating just how fucking unbearable one self-important asshole can become.

Now take your persecution complex, your worthless political legacy, and your bottomless reservoir of self-righteous horseshit, shove it all straight up your ass, and FUCK ALL THE WAY OFF, you pinecone-sucking, zero-accomplishment, traitor-ass motherfucker. 🖕
